Problem: Find the number such that the sum of its digits is equal to the difference between 328 and the sought number.

The arithmetic checks before the incorrect answer are correct: S(328)=13 with 328-328=0, S(199)=19 with 328-199=129, etc. None of the candidates tested before the false conclusion satisfies the equation.
This is false because the model had already correctly computed S(328)=13 and 328−328=0, so 328 does not satisfy the equation and cannot be the only solution.
Use S(x)=328−x to bound x by 301≤x≤328, since S(x)≤27 for a three-digit number, then test the remaining candidates systematically.
